data.name: Krati
data.gender_notes: Krati is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Krati is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kratu', which means 'power' or 'control'. In Hindu mythology, Krati is a feminine name associated with the goddess Kali, symbolizing the ultimate power and destructive force in the universe. The name Krati carries the meaning “Power, Control” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Krati usually hope their child will grow to embody power, control and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine power and strength.
data.etymology: Krati belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Power, Control.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Krati total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_sanskrit.name: क्रति
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: क्रतिः (kratih) is a Sanskrit word meaning power, strength, will, ability, authority. It is derived from the root verb क्रत् (kratah), which means to do, make, produce, accomplish, or establish. The suffix -ि (i) denotes a feminine gender. Thus, Krati is a feminine name meaning one who possesses great power or strength.

in_hindi.name: क्रति

data.cultural_impact: The name Krati is rooted in the rich Hindu culture and mythology. It holds a unique place in the Indian linguistic tradition and is esteemed for its deep meaning and significance. The name is also prevalent in some other Indian communities, albeit with slightly different meanings or variations in pronunciation. The naming of a child as Krati is believed to bestow upon them the blessings of strength, power, and self-control.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Krati is linked to the divine feminine and the goddess Kali. The goddess Kali embodies both the destructive and protective aspects of the divine, representing the powerful force of time and change, the unbearable grief, and the ultimate motherly love and compassion. Naming a child as Krati is believed to usher in the blessings of this powerful deity, ensuring that the child grows up with strength, determination, and a deep spiritual connection to the universe. The name is thus imbued with profound spiritual significance, empowering the child to overcome challenges, face adversities, and live a purposeful life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Krati, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kratu' meaning 'desire' or 'intention', symbolizes an individual deeply rooted in their purpose and driven by strong will and determination. spiritually, it represents the inner fire and commitment to manifest one's intentions into reality.

historical_references.reference: Krishna Dwaipayana Vyasa, the sage who compiled the Mahabharata, is also known as Krishna-Dwaipayana or Vyasa-Krishna. In this form, Krishna refers to the god Vishnu in his Krishna avatar, and Krishna-Dwaipayana or Vyasa-Krishna refers to Vyasa as the incarnation of the god Vishnu in human form, who authored the Mahabharata.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic containing 18 parvas or books, narrating the story of the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and Kaurava princes.

historical_references.reference: In the Puranic literature, Krati is mentioned as one of the seven horses or Saptamarthas of Indra, the king of the gods. These horses represent various aspects of Indra and are invoked in rituals to strengthen Indra's power. Krati is believed to represent Indra's strength, valor, and courage.
historical_references.context: Puranic literature is a genre of texts in Hinduism, which includes various scriptures, mythologies, and histories.
